Discharge path, bypassing the charge resistor. Anode on the bank: it conducts only once the rail has sagged a diode drop below the bank, which is exactly when the supply has gone away
Clamps harness-injected transients on the sensor 5V. 6.0V standoff, not 5.0V: a 5.0V part on a 5.0V rail leaks up to 800uA continuously

RX clamp. This one is not optional -- it conducts on every recessive bit above 11.5 V of battery, which is most of them
Protects the optional K-line pull-up only. The battery-sense divider is 100k and cannot pass enough current to matter

Pins 3/4 are the first CAN bus, always. Pins 5/6 are the second port and what they carry is a solder-jumper choice -- K-line on AUX_A, or the second CAN pair. Pin 1 is sense only: the board is powered from the dev board's USB-C, not from here

Mirrors DevKitC-1 J1. Pins 1-2 (3V3) and 21 (5V) are both INPUTS to the shield. Analog on 4-7 and 12, CAN on 9-11, SD bus on 15-20 -- grouped so each block routes away from the row rather than across it. Pin 3 is RST, pins 13/14 are IO3/IO46, all left open.

Mirrors DevKitC-1 J3. K-line on 4/5, the second CAN's SPI on 6-9 with its interrupt on 18, WS2812 on 16. Pin 17 is SD_PWR_EN, the one net that crosses to the other side of the board, and it goes round the end of the row. Pin 10 (IO38) is left open because it drives the dev board's RGB LED on v1.1; check the revision, some put it on IO48, which is the WS2812 output here.
External I2C sensors. Kept because the dev board has no Qwiic connector of its own
Shift-light header: +5V / 5V-logic DIN / GND
Push-pull socket; DET is the card-present switch
Two 5V excitation pins, two Kelvin sense-ground pins, two current-carrying grounds, four signals. SENS_RTN must land on the SENSOR's ground stud, not on the same stud as pins 9/10
The second ADC's unused pair, brought out raw -- 0-3.3V only, no divider and no clamp in front of them. For a bench sensor, not for the loom

Ships OPEN: unterminated. Bridge the pads only when this board is an END node on its own bus. A vehicle's bus -- OBD-II diagnostics included -- is already terminated at both ends, and a third 120 ohm across the pair takes it to about 40 ohm and can stop it working. Defaulting terminated made that an easy mistake to make
Ships OPEN. Bridge only if a module will not answer without a tester pull-up on the K-line
Ships OPEN, for the same reason TERM does: a vehicle bus is already terminated at both ends
Ships BRIDGED 1-2 = K-line on harness pin 5, which is what an R53 wants. For the second CAN instead: cut 1-2, bridge 2-3, and close AUXCL below. Both, or neither, is a bus that does not work

The second half of AUXSEL. Open in K-line mode, which also leaves the second transceiver looking at an open circuit -- harmless, but firmware must not enable CAN2 there or it will bus-off waiting for an ACK that cannot come

Inrush limit. 1206 for the pulse rating: 210 mA into 22 ohm is 1 W for the first instant, decaying with a 11 s time constant

Series limit. ISO 9141-2 wants the tester's dominant below 0.2*Vb: against the ECU's 510 ohm alone that is 12*33/543 = 0.73 V, and with the optional pull-up below also stuffed it is 1.38 V, both inside 2.4 V. Sized down from 100 ohm for exactly that second case. A sustained short of K-line to battery while transmitting puts 364 mA through the FET, over its 115 mA continuous rating -- it survives the pulse, not the fault. 1206 for the same reason
RX divider, upper leg
The ISO 9141-2 tester pull-up value. 1206: 12 V across it while the line is dominant is 280 mW
Ch1 series/fault-current limit; 0.1% thin film -- it is inside the divider chain, so its tolerance is a gain error
Ch1 bias resistor
Ch1 divider upper leg, 0.1% thin film for AFR-grade accuracy
Power-fail divider, upper leg

Ch1 divider lower leg. 2.21/13.21 = 0.1673, so 16.0 V in gives 2.68 V at the ADC and 5.0 V gives 0.836 V -- both inside the 3.1 V the ESP32 ADC can actually use. This value must match the return attenuator below exactly or the ground correction is worse than useless

Lower leg: trips at 1.24V * 40.7/12.0 = 4.20V. The rail sits at 4.5-4.7V loaded (USB 5 V less the dev board's Schottky and the cable drop), and the LDO above holds 3.3 V down to about 3.6 V in, so 4.20 is inside the margin at both ends
Divide by 13.2, not 11: at 36V the 11:1 divider put 3.27V on the pin, above the ADC's usable 3.1V, so the reading saturated near the top of the declared input window
Cathode pull-up. 10k gives the part 330uA, over the TLV431's 100uA minimum cathode current
Hysteresis, about 0.1 V at the rail. A USB rail is noisier than a battery and the trip point is only 300 mV below the working level, so this matters more here than it did on the parent

Power-fail comparator. Below the trip point it stops conducting and R_pu takes PWR_FAIL high, so the interrupt is a rising edge and an absent or dead part reads as 'failing' rather than as 'fine'. PINOUT: this uses KiCad's TL431DBZ numbering (1 K, 2 REF, 3 A) on a plain SOT-23. Shunt references are NOT consistent between vendors in this package -- CONFIRM against the datasheet for the exact part ordered. If REF and A are swapped the part simply never conducts and PWR_FAIL sits permanently asserted: loud, harmless, and obvious on the bench, but it will not be caught by ERC or DRC
5 V buffer so WS2812 DIN is a real 5 V rail, not 3.3 V hoping
Card-slot ESD clamp, CLK/CMD/D0/D1
5V bus drive with a 3.3V VIO pin, so no level shifting to the ESP32

Second CAN controller, on SPI. Pin 11 SDI is the controller's input, so it lands on the MCU's MOSI; pin 12 SDO is its output and lands on MISO -- naming them CAN2_MOSI/CAN2_MISO here keeps that straight, because SDI/SDO on a peripheral means the opposite of what it means on a host. VERIFY THE PART NUMBER against the live catalogue before ordering, as with every other line on this board
Channels 1-3. ADDR to GND = 0x48. Read AIN0-AIN3, AIN1-AIN3 and AIN2-AIN3: every one of them is a channel minus the shared sensor-ground reference
Channel 4, plus two spare differential inputs on the pads below. ADDR to +3V3 = 0x49
40 MHz, the top of the three rates the part accepts (4/20/40). Classic 500 kbit/s would be happy on 20, but 40 is what CAN FD data rates need and the crystals cost the same
